method: Independently read cached official court primary text at captions, claim-bearing factual and analysis paragraphs, and dispositions. Checked the ledger’s identity, dates, trial-versus-appellate attribution, reported reasoning, appellate outcome and source pinpoints. Matched every cited PDF hash. This was a substantive source review, not only schema validation.
limitations: This review does not certify a complete career docket or an exhaustive later appellate/trial history.
Case descriptions retain the source-ledger limitation that later proceedings are unknown unless expressly listed.
No overall ideology, retention recommendation, or party/Trump loyalty conclusion is supported by these selected cases.
No historical party claims appear in this subledger.
result: All 10 selected case groups verified; no substantive correction required.

records.findings: The appealed action is the 2024 summary dismissal, not attribution of the 2005 trial or sentence. The quoted trial order identifies missing medical support; the appellate court affirms and commends the written explanation.

The trial judge accepted consent to a search of the person but excluded the purse. Appellate consent-scope and officer-safety reasoning and affirmance match; the record contains no particularized suspicion.

Correctly separates Kane’s discretionary-impoundment finding and suppression from the appellate rejection. The no-appellee-brief / prima-facie-reversible-error posture is disclosed. Appellate opinion treated the later arrival of the co-owner as immaterial, including its uncertainty about proof of her license.

The respondent repeatedly refused in-person attendance, the court treated this as waiver and held a bench hearing. Trial concerns about observation and outside influence, independent plenary guardian, and appellate affirmance are supported. The source date is November 5, 2025.

records.findings: The $28,000.38 third-party negligent-misrepresentation judgment is correctly distinguished from the insurer’s separate recovery. Reversal rests on absence of duty to opposing litigant and thus no vicarious client liability.

sources.title: Auto-Owners Insurance Co. v. Konow, 2016 IL App (2d) 150823

records.findings: Tegeler heard the August 22, 2024 relief motion and adopted LoPiccolo’s initial findings; ledger does not assign him initial detention. Majority affirmed 2–1; McLaren’s dissent concerns intervening unfitness / mootness and available relief, not a merits conclusion that release was required.

The own action is dismissal of the amended successive petition for absence of cause. Neither the original 2000 sentence nor the appellate commentary on remorse is attributed to Villa. The cause barrier and counsel-assistance conclusions match.

records.findings: The 2024 caption names trial/sentencing judge Kliment, but paragraphs 5–12 expressly identify Flood’s July admonition and September in-absentia ruling. Supreme Court November 20, 2025 opinion unanimously reverses appellate judgment and affirms circuit result while directing full warnings in future. That later outcome is prominently preserved.
